method.method_draft: Use the incenter angle theorem. From the image, identify a triangle ABC with D inside the triangle, segments AD and DC drawn, and the angle at B labeled 50°. From the text, read that AD bisects angle BAC and DC bisects angle BCA, so D is the intersection of two internal angle bisectors, i.e., the incenter of triangle ABC. Apply the standard incenter fact: the angle between the bisectors to vertices A and C is ∠AIC = 90° + 1/2∠B. Therefore ∠ADC = 90° + 25° = 115°.
